summary: This paper compares two Ti3C2Tx-on-paper coplanar microsupercapacitor electrodes: HF-etched Ti3C2 MXene and LiF/HCl-derived clay-like Ti3C2 MXene. Both were deposited as 80:10:10 MXene/acetylene-black/PVDF slurries on Au-coated printing paper and laser-patterned into interdigitated electrodes. The clay-like Ti3C2 MXene is the headline and best-performing electrode, reaching 25 mF cm−2 at 20 mV s−1 in 1 m H2SO4, versus 6.2 mF cm−2 for HF-etched Ti3C2. No electrode-specific BET area, pore size, porosity, flake lateral size, tortuosity, gravimetric capacitance, or volumetric capacitance was reported.
